executive_brief: This document establishes a foundational technical constitution for a library-first software architecture. The core value relies on enforcing strict Test-Driven Development and CLI-first interfaces to guarantee independently testable, self-contained components. Data patterns follow a strict text I/O protocol (stdin/stdout) with structured logging for observability. Governance mandates that all pull requests verify compliance against these non-negotiable principles, ensuring architectural integrity over organizational convenience.

architectural_constraints: Every feature must start as a standalone, self-contained library with a clear purpose; organizational-only libraries are prohibited.
Every library must expose functionality via CLI using a strict text in/out protocol: stdin/args to stdout, errors to stderr.
TDD is mandatory and non-negotiable: tests must be written, user-approved, and fail before implementation begins; the Red-Green-Refactor cycle is strictly enforced.
Integration tests are mandatory for new library contract tests, contract changes, inter-service communication, and shared schemas.
Structured logging is required for observability and debuggability.
Versioning must strictly follow the MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD format.
Design must adhere to YAGNI principles and start simple.
All pull requests and code reviews must explicitly verify compliance with the constitution; any complexity must be justified.
Constitution amendments require formal documentation, approval, and a migration plan; the constitution supersedes all other practices.

maturity_assessment: The specification exhibits a highly stable and enforceable architectural baseline, successfully mapping all core principles, testing gates, and governance rules into a coherent dependency graph. The structural completeness is optimal, with only a single low-severity gap regarding the absence of an 'Open Questions & Uncertainties' section, which is expected for a foundational template. The project is fully READY for execution, providing a non-negotiable framework for library-first development and TDD enforcement.
